compute_signals.subproblem: Exhaustive enumeration of capsid–receptor binding signatures across engineered AAV libraries versus the BBB receptor panel (LY6A, LY6C1, ALPL, LRP6, CA4, AAVR) via docking, molecular dynamics, and AlphaFold-Multimer
compute_signals.what_compute_buys: Replaces the handful of published cryo-EM interfaces with a systematic map of contact-residue/loop-topology classes, potentially revealing shared geometric or energetic features of transcytosis-competent complexes (e.g., 3-fold-axis engagement of GPI-anchored receptors) and refining which binding signatures are candidates for BBB crossing.

compute_signals.subproblem: Supervised learning of transcytosis phenotype from joint (capsid sequence, receptor identity, structural, biophysical) features once paired transwell/in vivo labels are assembled
compute_signals.what_compute_buys: Converts class-level correlations into quantitative, variant-level predictors of transcytosis versus intracellular retention, ranks candidates for validation, and tests whether any computable binding-derived feature is actually predictive or whether trafficking variables dominate.

compute_signals.subproblem: Cross-species receptor–capsid compatibility scoring via comparative structural genomics of receptor orthologs and capsid interface conservation
compute_signals.what_compute_buys: Predicts translatability of a mouse-derived binding signature (e.g., LY6A-dependent PHP.eB) to human-relevant receptors (ALPL, LRP6), narrowing the search for conserved signatures and reducing failed NHP translation experiments.

options.id: Option 1: Exhaustive capsid–receptor complex enumeration (docking and AlphaFold-Multimer)
options.title: Exhaustive capsid–receptor complex enumeration (docking and AlphaFold-Multimer)
options.summary: Enumerate binding modes of engineered capsid libraries against the BBB receptor panel (LY6A, LY6C1, ALPL, LRP6, CA4, AAVR) with docking, MD refinement, and AlphaFold-Multimer to test whether transcytosis-competent pairs share a geometric motif such as 3-fold-axis engagement of GPI-anchored receptors (https://www.voyagertherapeutics.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/POSTER-Voyager_ASGCT_2024_FINAL_Ishan.pdf). Published modeling covers only single-digit complexes, e.g. AlphaFold-Multimer models of LRP6 with AAV-X1 and CAP-Mac VR-VIII peptides (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11381518), against an experimental catalog of ~150 AAV capsid structures (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12682079).
options.root_link: Bears on Q3 of the root question — for which capsid–receptor binding signatures transcytosis occurs — specifically whether a shared interface motif marks transcytosis-competent complexes.
options.compute_open: More parallel compute would buy model runs (capsid × receptor × pose); published measurements of its effect stop at single-digit numbers of AAV–receptor complexes modeled per study — two LRP6 peptide complexes in https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11381518 — and above that it is unknown whether exhaustive enumeration would surface a shared transcytosis-competent motif or demonstrate that no such motif exists.
options.sequential: none: every capsid–receptor pair is an independent docking or AlphaFold-Multimer job with its own random seeds, so the work already splits into independent pieces.
options.narrowing: This leaves aside everything after binding — endosomal sorting, lysosomal degradation, nuclear import — so the computed interface geometry stands in for the binding step alone, not for fate. Its answer still moves the root question because it either widens or closes the catalog of candidate signatures (Q3) against which the sufficiency claim (Q1) must be tested.

options.id: Option 2: Microsecond molecular dynamics of capsid–receptor–membrane assemblies
options.title: Microsecond molecular dynamics of capsid–receptor–membrane assemblies
options.summary: Run long MD of capsid plus receptor in a membrane at endosomal pH to watch binding poses, pH-triggered release, and raft/curvature effects: VCAP-102 binds ALPL at Kd ~20 nM at pH 7.4 but dissociates rapidly at pH 5.5 (https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.03.12.584703v1.full.pdf), and coarse-grained Martini3 simulations of AAV2 with AAVR in a model membrane reached microsecond frames with PKD1/PKD2 contacts lasting only ~1 µs at a time (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11492248).
options.root_link: Bears on Q1/Q3 — whether fate-relevant physics such as pH-dependent release and membrane-domain partitioning is already visible at the binding step, and so whether molecular mapping can be pushed toward a trafficking signature.
options.compute_open: settled: longer trajectories are already known to reveal more of the binding configurational space — the AAV2–AAVR coarse-grained study reports that once the capsid is membrane-bound its motion is restricted and much longer simulation times would be required to observe how the capsid moves on the membrane (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11492248).
options.sequential: One answer waits on a chain of ~2 fs integration steps (the timestep used in the AAV2–AAVR protocol, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11492248), each step consuming the previous step's forces and coordinates, so one 100 ns run is ~5×10^7 sequential steps and a 1 µs run ~5×10^8; the answer needs several independent replicas and a single replica keeps one GPU essentially fully busy (GPU offloading in gmx mdrun, https://manual.gromacs.org/documentation/current/user-guide/mdrun-performance.html). The steps must run in order inside one trajectory, but replicas can run at once and recasting the answer as an ensemble of many short trajectories combined by Markov-state analysis would let them run simultaneously — a payoff only if the dynamics is metastable so short runs recombine — as tried for virus capsid assembly with many short unbiased trajectories run in parallel (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1402.1784).
options.narrowing: This leaves aside the cell's sorting machinery — retromer/SNX tubule engagement, lysosomal routing — and treats simulated binding/unbinding and membrane partitioning as a stand-in for the trafficking decision. Its answer still moves the root question by testing whether any fate-relevant physics is recoverable from the binding step at all, which is exactly the sufficiency issue Q1 raises.

options.title: Supervised sequence-to-transcytosis phenotype models
options.summary: Train sequence-to-function models on paired (capsid features, transcytosis phenotype) data to rank variants for validation, following deep models that predicted AAV2 packaging viability from 201,426 assayed variants yielding 110,689 viable capsids (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41587-020-00793-4) and Fit4Function's six models trained on libraries of 240K variants or less that predicted macaque biodistribution (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11297966).
options.root_link: Bears on Q2 — assigning each variant a fate — and on whether the binding-to-fate gap in Q1 can be closed statistically instead of mechanistically.
options.compute_open: More parallel compute would buy model runs (seeds, architectures) and model size; published measurements of its effect stop at ensembles of three architectures over ~2×10^5 labeled variants (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41587-020-00793-4) and six Fit4Function models over ≤240K-variant libraries (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11297966), and above that it is unknown whether more parameters, seeds, or training compute improve transcytosis prediction or whether labeled transcytosis data, not FLOPs, is the binding constraint.
options.sequential: One training run is a chain of roughly 10^4–10^5 gradient updates, each update waiting on the previous weights' loss, so a converged answer needs multiple independent seeds and one model per trait (Fit4Function trained six, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11297966), and a single run keeps one GPU busy throughout. Within a run the updates must run in order, but different seeds and per-trait models can train at the same time — which pays off when each model fits one GPU and the labeled set is fully visible to every run, the arrangement used by Fit4Function's RNN/LSTM sequence models (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11297966).
options.narrowing: This leaves aside the mechanism of the sorting decision and treats a predicted transcytosis score as a stand-in for measured transwell/in vivo fate. Its answer still moves the root question because a predictor that generalizes would show which feature set carries fate information, i.e. how far Q3's signatures can be pushed toward Q1's sufficiency claim.

options.id: Option 4: Cryo-EM reconstruction of capsid–receptor complexes
options.title: Cryo-EM reconstruction of capsid–receptor complexes
options.summary: Determine single-particle cryo-EM structures of capsid–receptor complexes, as for AAV2–AAVR (PKD2) at 2.4 Å (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6561701), to extend the ~150-structure AAV capsid library (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12682079); all high-resolution cryo-EM structures of capsid complexes are single-particle reconstructions averaging large numbers of homogeneous particles (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12682079).
options.root_link: Bears on the interface-mapping component of Q1 — which capsid residues and receptor domains contact — that feeds the binding signatures of Q3.
options.compute_open: settled: map resolution is already known to improve as more particles contribute — in the AAV structural atlas, genome-containing AAV7/11/12/13 reconstructions reached slightly lower resolution than the empty capsids specifically because fewer capsids were used in those reconstructions (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7828300).
options.sequential: One map waits on a chain of processing stages — motion correction, CTF estimation, particle picking, 2D classification, 3D refinement — roughly a dozen sequential stages each consuming the previous stage's particle stack; the answer needs one reconstruction per complex plus re-runs for empty/full or symmetry-broken states (the AAV2 Rep–capsid work produced separate pentameric and hexameric maps, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12713660), and a single refinement keeps one GPU busy for hours to days. The stages must run in order, but per-particle work inside a stage can run simultaneously — as in local refinements of 45,150 and 75,559 symmetry-expanded particles on GPU computing resources (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12713660) — which pays off when a dataset holds tens of thousands of independent particles.
options.narrowing: This leaves aside affinity, kinetics, and post-binding sorting, so the static interface stands in for the whole binding event. Its answer still moves the root question because residue-level contact maps are the raw material from which any binding signature (Q3) is defined.

options.title: Cross-species receptor–capsid compatibility scoring
options.summary: Score capsid interfaces against receptor orthologs (ALPL, LRP6, AAVR, and mouse-restricted LY6A/LY6C1) to predict which signatures translate to humans: AlphaFold modeling of VCAP-102–ALPL predicted capsid-contacting ALPL residues conserved across human, cynomolgus macaque, and mouse (https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.03.12.584703v1.full.pdf), LRP6 emerged as a conserved BBB transcytosis receptor via interactome mapping plus AlphaFold-Multimer (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11381518), and LY6A/LY6C1 lack primate orthologs (https://journals.plos.org/plosbiology/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pbio.3002112).
options.root_link: Bears on the species-conditionality caveat of Q3 — whether a binding signature learned in mouse survives in human.
options.compute_open: More parallel compute would buy model runs (receptor-ortholog × capsid pairs scored); published measurements of its effect stop at a handful of isoforms — ALPL contact residues compared for one capsid across human, cynomolgus macaque, and mouse (https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.03.12.584703v1.full.pdf) — and above that it is unknown whether exhaustive ortholog scoring would keep, drop, or reorder the GPI-anchored-protein and LRP6 signatures as candidates for human BBB crossing.
options.sequential: none: each receptor-ortholog × capsid pair is an independent alignment and modeling job, so the work already splits into independent pieces.
options.narrowing: This leaves aside mouse-only biology such as Ly6a polymorphism underlying strain-specific PHP.B tropism (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31696742) and treats interface conservation as a stand-in for actual human transcytosis. Its answer still moves the root question because translatability is a necessary filter on any signature Q3 proposes for human use.
